messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency (<30 nmol/L) was associated with higher odds of depression compared with sufficient vitamin D among T2DM patients.
Sentence: "Multiple logistic regression analysis revealed that depression was significantly associated with older age (>60 years) (adjusted OR 2.04, 95% CI: 1.23-3.38), vitamin D deficiency (adjusted OR 4.24, 95% CI: 1.99-8.03), vitamin D insufficiency (adjusted OR 1.62, 95% CI: 1.19-2.71), and the use of both oral and injection medications (adjusted OR 1.86, 95% CI: 1.05-3.31)."
Measured as: depression (PHQ-9)
Population: 330 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Johor, Malaysia
Intervention: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level (deficient <30 nmol/L)
Comparator: Sufficient vitamin D (>50 nmol/L)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 330
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both bear on vitamin D and depression, but A is a single-arm case series of a combined D3/folate/B12 supplement in Parkinson's patients with a 15D depression dimension, while B is a cross-sectional association of low serum vitamin D with PHQ-9 depression in diabetics; the results differ in direction across design, population and intervention.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","comparator","outcome_measure"],"detail":"single-arm case series with combined supplement (D3 + folic acid + B12) vs cross-sectional serum-level association; Parkinson's vs type 2 diabetes; 15D dimension vs PHQ-9"}
